reason: The bearing frames should support the rotating crankshaft on the base.
expectation: The frames will attach to the base to support the shaft.

effect: The base now has bearings ready to support the shaft.
reason: The crankshaft belongs in the shaft bearings.
expectation: The crankshaft will fit into the bearings and turn on the base.

effect: The crankshaft is installed, so the cam can potentially turn with it.
reason: The off-centre cam should attach to the turning crankshaft to create the changing lift.
expectation: The cam will fit onto the crankshaft and rotate with it.

effect: The cam is installed, and its changing edge height can lift a follower as the shaft turns.
reaction: The comparison with a centred disc makes the mechanism clearer.
reason: The follower guide should hold the rod in line above the cam.
expectation: The guide will attach to the mechanism, ready to hold the follower rod.

effect: The guide fits onto the follower rod first, rather than directly onto the cam assembly.
reaction: That assembly order was not obvious to me.
reason: The guided follower should now fit onto the cam mechanism so the cam can move the rod.
expectation: The follower assembly will attach above the cam.

effect: The guided follower is now positioned over the cam.
reaction: The assembly is taking shape as expected.
reason: The follower spring should help keep the rod against the cam as it turns.
expectation: The spring will attach to the follower mechanism.

effect: The spring is fitted, and testing can compare its pull with an unhooked run.
reaction: I am curious what difference the spring makes.
reason: The removable crank handle should let me turn and test the assembled lifter.
expectation: The handle will fit onto the crankshaft and allow the mechanism to be tested.

effect: The completed test showed that the spring keeps the follower against the cam, making its downward movement reliable as well as its lift.
reaction: The comparison with and without the spring was a satisfying explanation of why it matters.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the finished lifter was most worthwhile: seeing the follower hang without the spring explained a real mechanism rather than just completing an assembly.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bearings and shaft was straightforward but less informative than seeing how the cam and spring work.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the light follower sometimes hangs without the spring's pull.

arbitrary.text: The guide's assembly order was not obvious: I expected it to attach to the mechanism rather than the rod first, although the compatibility feedback resolved it.

continue.text: Yes. The cam and spring demonstrations made me curious to see how the mechanism will animate the paper dragon.
